quotes.text: A virtual table is a table definition inside dataverse that points to records stored somewhere else.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: A crisp one-sentence definition of virtual tables.

quotes.text: People often ask for one system when what they really need is one place to work. Those are two different things.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Reframes integration requirements around user experience rather than data consolidation.

quotes.text: Before you expose customer, Finance or stock data through a Virtual Table, ask a direct question. When a user opens this record, which system checks their permission?
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: A practical security check before exposing external data in Dynamics 365.

quotes.text: You can't turn a Virtual Table into a standard Dataverse Table later, and you can't take a standard Table and switch it into a Virtual One.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Highlights a permanent design decision that is easy to overlook.

quotes.text: If another system owns the Data and your team just needs a live view while working in Dynamics 365, use a Virtual Table. Think of it as a window, you see through it, but nothing gets copied.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: A clear decision rule for choosing virtual tables over a synced copy.

Choosing a window or a local copy

takeaways: Dataverse virtual tables, formerly virtual entities, show live external data in Dynamics 365 without storing a second copy, so the source system keeps ownership.
Every virtual table relies on a data provider that translates requests, a data source that points to the external service, and a table definition that maps columns and GUID IDs.
Virtual tables don't support Dataverse auditing, search, charts, offline use or calculated columns, depend on the source for security and speed, and can't be converted later, so choose deliberately.
hook: When stock levels live in a warehouse system and invoices in finance, copying everything into Dynamics 365 creates stale numbers, duplicates and fragile sync jobs. This Simply Explained episode helps Dynamics 365 and Power Platform makers, admins and architects understand virtual tables, formerly virtual entities. Learn how providers and data sources work, where virtual tables fit, and when a local copy is still the better choice.
